title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: Player Two's Anglo-Saxon leader is a generic KING unit rather than a named hero; the engine offers no Harold Godwinson, so this is defensible, but Harold is textually named while being represented by an anonymous monarch figure

Full economic/military infrastructure (TOWN_CENTER, BARRACKS, STABLE, ARCHERY_RANGE, BLACKSMITH, MONASTERY) for both sides on a one-day pitched battlefield near Hastings; neither army had settlements or production facilities on Senlac ridge (William's only fixed work was the motte at Hastings, miles away)
GOLD_MINE x5 and STONE_MINE x4 plus forage bushes and livestock as harvestable resources on what should be a purely tactical battlefield map
'Norman Reinforcements' trigger creating fresh riders 'from the coast' — William committed his whole force; no reinforcement column arrived during the battle
2560 oak trees on a 120x120 map produces a heavily forested field, whereas Senlac was an open ridge with cultivated slopes and only marshy ground and scattered woodland (the Malfosse) at the flanks

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Norman/Anglo-Saxon architecture and unit bonuses are unassigned — a Frankish (Norman) vs Briton/Celt (Saxon) pairing was available and avoidable

2,560 oak trees on a 120x120 map turns Senlac into dense forest; the historical field was open downland with a ridge and marshy ground, and heavy woods contradict the cavalry manoeuvre and feigned-retreat tactics the brief centres on
Both armies are given permanent economic/production bases (TOWN_CENTER, BARRACKS, STABLE, ARCHERY_RANGE, BLACKSMITH, MONASTERY) for a single-day set-piece battle where neither side built anything
The 'Norman Reinforcements' trigger invents fresh riders arriving from the coast; William received no reinforcements at Hastings — his whole force was committed from the start
Force ratio is inverted: 30 Norman units (only 10 knights) against 51 Saxons, whereas the armies were roughly equal in size and the Norman advantage lay in its large mounted and archer contingents
Harold is represented by an unrenamed generic KING unit; since the engine ships no Harold hero this is an acceptable stand-in, but leaving it unnamed weakens identification
No archer arm for the Saxons is correct, but the Saxon SKIRMISHER count (10) reads as missile troops the shield wall largely lacked

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Norman and Anglo-Saxon architecture and unit bonuses are left to chance — the engine offers Franks/Britons (or Vikings/Celts) as obvious, avoidable choices for 1066 Normandy and England.

2,560 TREE_OAK on a 120x120 map turns Senlac Hill into dense forest; Hastings was fought on an open ridge above a shallow valley, and heavy woods also make the scripted downhill pursuit/feigned-retreat manoeuvre geographically implausible.

Harold Godwinson is represented by a KING unit — a non-combatant with no attack — rather than a renamed CHAMPION or a Teutonic/Frankish infantry hero; the historical Harold fought and died in the shield wall.

Player 2 receives 10 SKIRMISHERS; Anglo-Saxon missile troops were negligible at Hastings, and the engine's spearmen/champions alone would have represented the housecarl-and-fyrd shield wall more faithfully.
The 'Norman Reinforcements' trigger inventing 'fresh Norman riders arrive from the coast' is not attested; no reinforcements reached William during the battle — his whole force was already engaged.

Gold mines, stone mines, forage bushes and a full economic building set (Town Center, Blacksmith, Stable, Archery Range, Monastery) for both sides imply a settled base-building contest rather than a single-day pitched battle between an invasion camp and a marching army.
